resources.string: Cross-section of a simplified synovial joint. Not all joints are synovial. The joint space is widened for clarity.
The outer fibrous wall surrounds the joint and joins the two bones. It is thicker than the synovial lining on its inner face.
This thin membrane lines the inside of the capsule up to the cartilage margins. It does not cover the articular surfaces.
This is normally a narrow space containing a small amount of lubricating synovial fluid, not a wide, empty gap between the bones.
In this example, a thin coat of hyaline cartilage covers each facing bone surface. The two coats face each other across the joint space but are not joined.
The capsule attaches to bone outside the smooth, cartilage-covered surfaces, leaving those surfaces free to glide past each other.
